text:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall (marco) — SEV2: sustained p99 latency spike for egress LB in us-west2. Alerts: router->egress p99 > 1.8s for last 5m, streaming stalls reported.
marco: on it. joining bridge. any customer impact visible?
sasha: seeing a big increase in tail for streaming sessions (p99 ~2.1s, p95 ~450ms). non-streaming generation p99 up to 900ms. lots of retries from mobile clients.
li: ops metrics: traffic shifted heavily to a small set of shards in us-west2 (hot partitions). LB routing table shows affinity weight skew after the 02:14 deploy.
tayla: did a routing policy change roll out minutes before spike — deploy ID: rollout-2026-03-15-0212. 
marco: marking the deploy as suspect. can we rollback policy to previous seed? if risky, maybe disable affinity and force round-robin as mitig.
derek: I can flip the ingress-lb affinity -> off for us-west2 for a quick mitigation. pulling runbook: Route Mitigation (runbook ref).
cs-ops: customer telemetry: three paid customers reported stream interruptions, one on-prem high-throughput ingest saw repeated reconnects. Not yet a formal support escalation but likely to become one.
marco: ok execute mitigations in order: 1) disable affinity in us-west2, 2) temporarily increase egress pool capacity for us-west2, 3) enable fallback to smaller model variants for streaming if latency > 1s. Derek please run 1.
derek: running: `kubectl -n infra exec -it lb-configurator -- ./lbctl set-affinity --region=us-west2 --enabled=false`
derek: (output) `OK: affinity disabled for us-west2 (seed rollback deferred)`
li: routing telemetry updating — weight skew dropping in the next two minutes, p99 trending down.
sasha: p99 dropped to 1.2s at 02:21, p95 back to ~380ms. streaming stalls still occasional but much reduced.
marco: good. create a short postmortem checklist for whether to rollback rollout-2026-03-15-0212 or patch policy. What caused the skew?
li: preliminary: new seed algorithm introduced an ordering bug for shard weight compaction causing a small subset of shards to get majority of traffic when certain key-heat thresholds hit. Hot partitions amplified latency because those shards were CPU-bound on KV cache misses.
sasha: observed KV cache miss rate spike on the hot shards — cache thrash. Also some long GC cycles on a subset of router pods coincident with the traffic surge.
marco: are we seeing cross-region fallback spamming clients? any cascade?
derek: no wide cascade. most traffic stayed in region; smart routing didn't trigger fallback because capacity looked available (but concentrated). fallback rules are fine.
cs-ops: customers affected: cust-alpha (streaming), cust-gamma (embeddings), both on us-west2. CS is preparing proactive outreach.
marco: assign action owners: li investigate compaction bug and produce a patch (ETA 4h). sasha to collect evals and perf tests replicating hot-partition pattern (ETA 3h). derek to run capacity tuning & monitor (ongoing). tayla to coordinate support comms.
li: spinning up targeted perf test: synthetic traffic reproducing skew pattern. snippet: ```python
# stress script (excerpt)
for i in range(100000):
    key = f\"user:{random.choice(hot_keys)}\"
    client.request(model="stream-v1", key=key)
```
marco: good. also capture heap/GC traces for the router pods that had high p99. attach logs.
sasha: logs (redacted): ```
router-7f8b: latency spike: tail=2100ms, gc_pause=120ms, kv_miss_rate=0.46
router-a12c: latency normal: tail=120ms, gc_pause=20ms, kv_miss_rate=0.05
```
derek: increased egress pool by +2 GPUs in us-west2 (hotpool-2) as temporary capacity buffer. watch dashboards for the next 30m.
marco: monitoring: p99 now ~680ms at 02:38, p95 ~300ms. still some small streaming stalls but acceptable for now. keep page open for 1h.
cs-ops: flagged support cases and added incident tag. prepping customer notes: affected windows 02:14-02:22 UTC, mitigation applied 02:19 UTC.
tayla: drafting message for customers: short apology, what happened, mitigation, follow-up patch ETA.
marco: next steps: - do a targeted rollback only if patch ETA > 8h or we see a regression after affinity flip - collect flamegraphs for affected router pods - add safety throttle to compaction algorithm (temp config) - schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
li: found root repro: in compaction path, under heavy key collision the algorithm truncated weight buckets incorrectly leading to seed bias. small fix ready, will run unit+integration tests.
sasha: once fix lands, we should canary in a single region with traffic shaping to detect recurrence before a global rollout.
derek: baseline checklist completed. removing the emergency page but keeping a watch channel. moving to post-incident triage. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (affinity disabled + capacity increase). severity: SEV2 -> monitoring.
marco: closing bridge in 10. thanks everyone. please add your notes to the incident doc and tag follow-ups.
cs-ops: filing customer-impact summary to the incident tracker and pinging account managers.
marco: good job. we'll reconvene for a 1hr scrub if new anomalies show up.
